additional_info.body:
Dear Johan,
Thank you for your feedback regarding the charger.
We have checked the charging sessions you have mentioned, and see that the charging sessions stopped normally, because the battery of the car was 100%.
The issue you are mentioning, is a communication problem between the EV and the charger. The charger has a delay of communication at that moment, and receives updates from inside the charger, which has no effect on the charging session going on. This also shows in the logs.
A delay of communication inside the charger, shows this message.
We hope to have informed you enough.
Please provide us with feedback, so we can close the ticket.
Thank you.
Kind regards,
Priscilla van Wettum

additional_info.subject: ID0484204/DC/Si-D/SE-[RVP/T4 170004780] Charging Station Operational Issues CRM:03209000375
additional_info.body:
Hi Johan, good morning.
Here is the analysis from Wednesday with the EV:
ec.94.68.00.1b.d6 - keeping in mind we used the same connector for all sessions.
These tests below were performed always in the same EV Inlet which we will call Inlet1.
At 12:00 (UTC) we started a session succesfully right at the start, without any issues:
As you can see we have a difference of ~8V and still go through with it without any drop.
We stopped the session and started a new one. When we reach PreCharge, we reach the Voltage in <3sec:
After we reach the voltage, the EV doesn't move to PowerDeliveryReq and we see a voltage drop:
The 3rd attempt was the same behaviour.
At the 4th attempt the charging worked perfectly again and from there onwards for the next 3 sessions, no session were failed.
Now, we moved to the 2nd Inlet of the EV and could only do 2 sessions due to the necessity of operations.
The first session is the same behaviour of the drop of voltage:
For these sessions we enabled the .pcap traces collection and from the logs we keep seeing PreChargeRequests even though we reach the voltage:
And then the TCP connection drop from EV side.
The 2nd session worked perfectly well.
From our point of view, using our remote software to check the hardware faults and the logs, the fault doesn't seem to lie on our side. What we believe is that the EV is not closing the contactors properly, or not reading the PreCharge voltage correctly and stopping the session.
Can you please reach out to Mercedes with this information? We are open to discussion and if needed another remote session, it's just a matter of aligning a date. You can reply to this email with their email or contact for us to reach out.
Thank you very much for your help on site and have a nice weekend.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: Sv: ID0484204/DC/Si-D/SE-[RVP/T4 170004780] Charging Station Operational Issues CRM:03209000375
additional_info.body:
Hi,
This is the answer from Mercedes Germany:
The following was determined during this process:
The charger fails to stabilize the voltage at our EV target voltage of 761 V or 762 V during pre-charge and at times drops
(The minimum value was approximately 680 V)
As a result, EV-Ready then switches from TRUE to FALSE and charging is aborted.
This means that the power supply on the charger fluctuates too much
Med vänlig hälsning,
Johan Wennerstrand
Kalkyl

Utmaningen med avbruten laddning på Bengts Åkeri
Hej Johan,
Hoppas allt väl!
Tack för trevligt samtal.
Se mina kommentarer nedan…
Utmaningen med kompabilitet mellan Siemens och eActros är inte isolerat till Sverige och Bengts Åkeris laddare och fordon i Örebro. Utmaningarna mellan just Siemens laddare och eActros existerar på många europeiska marknader och är idag välkänt hos både Siemens och Daimler Trucks
Det pågår felsökning och analys både gemensamt och individuellt hos både Siemens och Daimler Trucks
Utmaningen med felsökningsarbetet just nu är att laddproblemen uppstår inte hela tiden. Därför är det svårt att hitta mönster avseende fel/orsaker
Vi kommer inom kort att montera en ”data-logger” på en av Bengts Åkeris fordon för att ännu bättre extrahera fordonsdata och.., med support av Damiler Trucks.., analysera större mängder data och den vägen se om vi kan finna möjliga orsaker tillsammans med Siemens
Jag har fått information från ansvarig säljare på Veho Truck Retail att ni varit i kontakt med Bengts Åkeri vid flertalet tillfällen och eventuellt gjort uppdateringar på laddaren. Jag är intresserad av att veta mer exakt vad ni har gjort? Era insatser blir en viktig del i den interna dialogen med Daimler Trucks
och den externa dialogen med Siemens.

additional_info.subject: NOTE FROM L3 - Translation
additional_info.body:
The challenge with compatibility between Siemens and eActros is not isolated to Sweden and Bengts Åkeris' charger and vehicle in Örebro. The challenges between Siemens chargers and eActros exist in many European markets and are now well known to both Siemens and Daimler Trucks
Troubleshooting and analysis are ongoing both jointly and individually at both Siemens and Daimler Trucks
The challenge with the troubleshooting work right now is that the charging problems do not occur all the time. Therefore, it is difficult to find patterns regarding errors/causes
We will soon install a "data logger" on one of Bengts Åkeri's vehicles to even better extract vehicle data and.., with support from Damiler Trucks.., analyze larger amounts of data and that way see if we can find possible causes together with Siemens
I have received information from the responsible salesperson at Veho Truck Retail that you have been in contact with Bengts Åkeri on several occasions and possibly made updates to the charger. I am interested in knowing more exactly what you have done? Your efforts will be an important part of the internal dialogue with Daimler Trucks and the external dialogue with Siemens.

Yes this is true but the symptom and root cause are very different - this “known issue” is related to a noise in the CP line created by the EV due to the air pump used to cool the batteries during high power charging which has been acknowledged by Daimler, we also developed a hotfix for this where we are less strict with the PilotState measurements and so far, the tests show good results, as you say, below, the tests are being performed together with Daimler HQ themselves.
Troubleshooting and analysis are ongoing both jointly and individually at both Siemens and Daimler Trucks
See above - correct
The challenge with the troubleshooting work right now is that the charging problems do not occur all the time. Therefore, it is difficult to find patterns regarding errors/causes
Well this is true for a specific set of EVs, I did a pre analysis a couple of weeks ago and found that there is one EV which has many more failures than others which is this EVCCID:
ec.94.68.00.1b.d6
, which is also the one we used for testing, and in the first attempts we fail 2 or 3 times before the rest of the times work fine. We can use this one for testing in my opinion.
We will soon install a "data logger" on one of Bengts Åkeri's vehicles to even better extract vehicle data and.., with support from Damiler Trucks.., analyze larger amounts of data and that way see if we can find possible causes together with Siemens
We also have involved our R&D team for further support. I already discussed this with the colleague that got assigned and let's align on a date to test and collect every information possible.
I have received information from the responsible salesperson at Veho Truck Retail that you have been in contact with Bengts Åkeri on several occasions and possibly made updates to the charger. I am interested in knowing more exactly what you have done? Your efforts will be an important part of the internal dialogue with Daimler Trucks and the external dialogue with Siemens.
As far as I know, we only updated the charger to the latest version and included the hotfix about the PilotState above, since in the beginning of the report, we weren't able to record the .pcap files and as such, we didn't have a clear understanding of what was wrong.
Now that we have the .pcap files and some recordings of our own hardware system, we can confirm that the problem seems to lie in the PreCharge phase like Daimler previously mentioned where the voltage of the charger doesn't stabilize.
Right now, we don't have a clear root cause on why the voltage is not stabilizing and I have 2 theories at the moment:
The charger is not keeping the voltage on the required value → I need R&D support to find the root cause and how to fix it.
EV is not closing the contactors properly → that's why we wanted Daimler to support us as well.
I am just thinking of all the possibilities since in PreCharge there are not too many participants, since we are able to pass CableCheck as well, if the problem is within our charger we will gladly provide a fix.
Thank you very much for your time and availability and feel free to answer to this email if you have any questions or doubts.
Have a nice weekend!
Best regards,
Francisco
